study: Heller et al. 2010 (SREE), WestEd Making Sense of SCIENCE PD (electric circuits)
eval_evidence: Conducted by WestEd / Heller Research Associates, the developers of the Making Sense of SCIENCE courses (authors Heller, Daehler, Shinohara are WestEd staff); NSF-funded but developer-conducted, not an independent third-party evaluation.
developer_evidence: Courses were 'delivered by professionals in the field (not the course developers)'; local course facilitators drawn from each site delivered the PD (the journal version: 'Interventions were delivered by staff developers trained to lead the teacher courses in their regions'), with the SF Bay Area as a partial exception where developers were solo facilitators.
cascade_evidence: Local facilitators were trained at WestEd to lead the courses in their regions, then delivered them to teachers: developer -> trained local facilitator -> teacher (>=1 extra hop). Train-the-trainer style delivery by design.
counterfactual_evidence: Fourth condition was a no-treatment control; control teachers received no PD (and were offered the course the following summer). Business-as-usual, no active alternative.
coaching_evidence: Each course was eight three-hour sessions completed over 8-14 weeks during the school year (or a 5-day summer block); a face-to-face course/workshop format with no ongoing in-class coaching of teachers in their own classrooms.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention targets teachers' science content/pedagogical knowledge for teaching the existing electric-circuits unit; only the teacher's regular instruction changes, no added student-facing dose.
maturity_evidence: The PD course is a single-year (one course completion) intervention; student content-test outcomes measured in the immediate study year (gain within two weeks of completing the unit). No multi-year maturity axis for the core contrast (a separate follow-up-year cohort exists but is a different student sample).
